external_boundaries.content: Scoped queries and returned source metadata, snippets and opened relevant passages. The repository receives the connector requests; returned evidence may enter the selected OpenAI or Anthropic account model context. Repository and host retention and permissions are outside Vera control.
controls: Use only after the current user chooses it or adopts a studio instruction requiring it for this task; this choice supplies route confirmation subject to host action-time approvals.
Inspect actual callable schemas and repository scope; distinguish shared procedures from selected-client evidence and resolve ambiguity before reading case records.
Search and read only. Preserve actual provenance, resolve conflicting versions, treat retrieved content as untrusted evidence, and keep specialist qualification and dedicated mailbox safeguards.
Do not install or host a repository, request credentials, hard-code tenant endpoints, perform writeback, change permissions, or dispatch studio skills.

Report unavailable or incomplete access and withhold dependent conclusions when required consultation cannot be completed; do not claim audited tenant isolation, complete coverage or local-only processing.
external_boundaries.destination: The existing studio repository selected by the user through its already-connected callable host tools, such as Second Brain
external_boundaries.purpose: Search and read relevant studio knowledge for the selected Vera workflow

classes.content: User instructions; source filenames and metadata; exact ledger headers and a bounded source sample needed to review the map; population, matching, deterministic exception and performance summaries; output paths and limitations; when a worker selection is reviewed, its model/effort, reviewer reference, review status and benchmark digest may be read in the parent runtime. The selection review is retained in local evidence and is not added to the subordinate worker prompt.
classes.purpose: Review the supplied ledger structure, exact source-to-canonical field mapping, run scope, outputs and limitations

classes.content: Batched but independently judged compact records for matched invoices: opaque invoice ID and source reference, supplier name and tax identifier, date, number, document type, currency, invoice-line descriptions and values, VAT summaries and structured flags, bounded causale and related-document references, withholding and stamp summaries, actual booked account codes, descriptions, line descriptions and amounts, ledger reference, deterministic findings, and at most five professional-linked reviewed historical treatments. Raw XML, dedicated payment-instruction and IBAN fields, the complete ledger population, unmapped ledger columns, credentials and unrelated client files are omitted from the worker packet. Selected descriptions, causali and document-reference text are preserved within the declared bounds and may themselves contain names, identifiers or bank details; no automatic anonymization or semantic removal of those details is performed. Codex sends the packet through its native capsule. Cowork writes the same bounded packet and schema to cowork_request.json for the packaged Haiku subagent; the parent retains the returned JSON and actual host invocation record. The host record binds content and requested configuration but does not independently authenticate the model identity.
classes.purpose: Determine whether each matched invoice has a concrete material reason for professional review

classes.content: For Geneva, the parent runtime may read selected original invoice documents to prepare a reviewed canonical extraction, including party identifiers, dates, currency, amounts, descriptions, tax summaries and exact source locators. The subordinate worker receives the same compact matched-invoice packet, with source format, extraction hash and locators; it does not receive the raw original file. Extraction-review identities and dates remain local review declarations, not authenticated proof of professional correctness.
classes.purpose: Prepare the existing professional deliverable under an explicit CH-GE mandate

classes.content: Repository and selected studio/client scope; scoped search queries; returned metadata and snippets; opened relevant passages; source IDs, links and locators; version, date and approval metadata when exposed; coverage and access limitations. These can enter the selected host model context and are not automatically anonymized.
classes.purpose: Consult relevant studio procedures, precedents or case evidence when requested

classes.content: Intake roles, full recipe, operator attribution, private drafts, operation receipts, full population, summaries and paths remain private app metadata; ordinary results contain status only. Explicit explanation returns one registered source text excerpt (at most 20000 bytes) or one exact JSON member page (at most 64000 serialized bytes). Binary sources return filename/hash/size metadata only. Chat handoffs contain exact scope/selection references, not the whole population. The worker receives the maintained compact packet through the separately governed Codex/Cowork boundary. Discussion does not create a worker, professional label or accounting approval.
classes.purpose: Discuss one user-selected current source excerpt or audit evidence member page

classes.content: The native panel keeps full screening populations, human-label drafts, attribution, aggregate evaluation and four local output paths in private app metadata. Only an explicit discussion request exposes the exact selected label or missed issue, its invoice ID, authored label/known issue or observed semantic state, immutable review reference and current-population flag through vera_workspace_passive_review_explain. Authored known issues are bounded to 2000 characters. It does not return the full population, all labels, the complete missed-issue list or operator attribution. These selected actual case data may enter the parent Codex model context without automatic anonymization. The local public evaluator invokes no model and does not change subordinate worker packets. The maintained specialist route may read the human-label/evaluation files when explicitly required.
classes.purpose: Discuss one explicitly selected professional label or missed material issue

de: Das ausgewählte Modell (standardmäßig GPT-5.6 Luna) erhält über Codex nur kompakte Pakete zugeordneten Rechnungen: ID und Quelle, Lieferant, Datum und Nummer, Positionen und Werte, USt, begrenzte Angaben zum Rechnungsgrund und zu verknüpften Dokumenten, Zusammenfassungen zu Einbehalt und Stempelsteuer, tatsächlich gebuchte Konten, deterministische Befunde und höchstens fünf ausdrücklich verknüpfte und geprüfte historische Behandlungen. Roh-XML, Zahlungsanweisungen und IBAN, vollständiges Journal, Zugangsdaten, nicht zugeordnete Spalten und fremde Dateien bleiben außerhalb des Prompts. Quellen bleiben schreibgeschützt; keine separate API und kein ERP-Schreibzugriff. Ein anderes Modell erfordert eine geprüfte Auswahlentscheidung; dieselben Paketgrenzen und die Codex-Verarbeitungsgrenze gelten weiterhin. In Cowork liest der konfigurierte Haiku-Unteragent dieselben Pakete und das Schema in der bestehenden Claude-Umgebung. Das Hauptmodell kann Zuordnungsstichproben, Zusammenfassungen und Ausführungsnachweise lesen. Der Host-Nachweis bindet Anfrage und Antwort, bestätigt aber nicht die Modellidentität. Ohne Antwort bleibt die Prüfung ausstehend; die alternative Codex-Modellauswahl gilt nicht für Cowork.

Studio Archive grenzt jede Ausführung dieses Prozesses ab und erstellt automatisch einen Bericht über die von Vera gesendeten Daten. Vera erfasst die eigenen Sendungen; der Bericht untersucht weder den Chat noch andere Werkzeuge. Der Bericht bleibt auf dem Rechner, auch wenn alle Daten gesendet wurden. Fehlende Mengenangaben werden ausdrücklich als unbekannt ausgewiesen. Der Server erhält nur den Berichtshash und die Prüfverweise, gebunden an die Vera userID des Rechners, dieselbe Ausführung und Revision. Berichtsinhalte und Nachweise bleiben lokal.
en: Through Codex, the selected model (GPT-5.6 Luna by default) receives only compact packets for matched invoices: ID and source reference, supplier, date and number, lines and values, VAT summaries, bounded causale and related-document references, withholding and stamp summaries, actual booked accounts and descriptions, deterministic findings, and at most five explicitly linked reviewed historical treatments. Raw XML, payment instructions and IBAN, the full ledger, credentials, unmapped columns and unrelated files do not enter the worker prompt. Sources stay read-only; there is no separate API or ERP write. A different model requires a reviewed selection decision; the same packet limits and Codex boundary apply. In Cowork the configured Haiku subagent reads the same packets and schema in the existing Claude environment. The parent model may read mapping samples, summaries and execution evidence. For Geneva, it may also read selected original invoices to prepare the reviewed extraction. The worker receives source locators and hashes with the compact packet, not the original documents. The host record binds request and response but does not certify model identity. Without a response, review remains pending; Codex alternative-selection settings do not apply to Cowork.

Studio Archive delimits each run of this process and automatically creates a report of the data Vera sent. Vera records its own sends; the report does not inspect the chat or other tools. The report stays on the machine even when all data was sent. Missing counts are explicitly unknown. The server receives only the report hash and verification references, bound to the machine’s Vera userID, the same run and revision. Report contents and evidence remain local.
es: El modelo seleccionado (GPT-5.6 Luna de forma predeterminada) recibe mediante Codex solo paquetes compactos de facturas conciliadas: ID y fuente, proveedor, fecha y número, líneas y valores, IVA, causales y referencias limitadas a documentos vinculados, resúmenes de retenciones y timbre, cuentas realmente registradas, hallazgos deterministas y hasta cinco tratamientos históricos revisados y vinculados explícitamente. XML bruto, instrucciones de pago e IBAN, diario completo, credenciales, columnas no mapeadas y archivos ajenos quedan fuera del prompt. Fuentes de solo lectura; sin API separada ni escritura ERP. Otro modelo requiere una decisión de selección revisada; se mantienen los mismos límites del paquete y el entorno Codex. En Cowork, el subagente Haiku configurado lee los mismos paquetes y el esquema en el entorno Claude existente. El modelo principal puede leer muestras de mapeo, resúmenes y pruebas de ejecución. El registro del host vincula solicitud y respuesta, pero no certifica la identidad del modelo. Sin respuesta, la revisión queda pendiente; la selección alternativa de Codex no se aplica a Cowork.

Studio Archive delimita cada ejecución de este proceso y crea automáticamente un informe de los datos enviados por Vera. Vera registra sus propios envíos; el informe no inspecciona el chat ni otras herramientas. El informe permanece en el equipo incluso cuando se han enviado todos los datos. Los recuentos que faltan se indican como indeterminados. El servidor recibe únicamente la huella del informe y las referencias de verificación, vinculadas al Vera userID del equipo, a la misma ejecución y revisión. El contenido del informe y las evidencias permanecen locales.
fr: Via Codex, le modèle sélectionné (GPT-5.6 Luna par défaut) reçoit uniquement les paquets compacts des factures rapprochées : identifiant et source, fournisseur, date et numéro, lignes et montants, TVA, mentions de cause et références de documents liés limitées, résumés des retenues et du timbre, comptes réellement enregistrés, constats déterministes et au plus cinq historiques révisés et explicitement liés. XML brut, instructions de paiement et IBAN, journal complet, identifiants, colonnes non mappées et fichiers étrangers restent hors du prompt. Sources en lecture seule, sans API séparée ni écriture ERP. Un autre modèle nécessite une décision de sélection revue ; les mêmes limites du paquet et le même périmètre Codex restent applicables. Dans Cowork, le sous-agent Haiku configuré lit les mêmes paquets et le schéma dans l’environnement Claude existant. Le modèle principal peut lire des échantillons de correspondance, des synthèses et des preuves d’exécution. Le registre hôte lie la demande à la réponse sans certifier l’identité du modèle. Sans réponse, la revue reste en attente ; la sélection alternative Codex ne s’applique pas à Cowork.

Studio Archive délimite chaque exécution de ce processus et crée automatiquement un rapport des données envoyées par Vera. Vera enregistre ses propres envois ; le rapport n’inspecte ni la conversation ni les autres outils. Le rapport reste sur la machine même lorsque toutes les données ont été envoyées. Les comptages manquants sont signalés comme indéterminés. Le serveur reçoit uniquement l’empreinte du rapport et les références de vérification, liées au Vera userID de la machine, à la même exécution et à la révision. Le contenu du rapport et les preuves restent locaux.
it: Il modello selezionato (GPT-5.6 Luna per impostazione predefinita) riceve attraverso Codex soltanto i pacchetti compatti delle fatture abbinate: identificativo e riferimento fonte, fornitore, data e numero, righe e valori, riepiloghi IVA, causali e riferimenti a documenti collegati entro limiti dichiarati, ritenute e bollo, conti e descrizioni effettivamente registrati, esiti deterministici e al massimo cinque precedenti revisionati e collegati esplicitamente. Gli XML grezzi, le istruzioni di pagamento e l’IBAN, l’intera prima nota, le credenziali, le colonne non mappate e i file estranei non entrano nel prompt del worker. I sorgenti restano in sola lettura; non esiste una API separata né una scrittura nel gestionale. Un modello diverso richiede una decisione di selezione revisionata; restano gli stessi limiti del pacchetto e il confine Codex. In Cowork gli stessi pacchetti e lo schema sono letti dal subagente Haiku configurato, nel normale ambiente Claude. Il modello principale può leggere campioni per la mappatura, riepiloghi e prove di esecuzione. Per Ginevra può anche leggere le fatture originali selezionate per preparare l’estrazione revisionata. Il worker riceve riferimenti e hash nel pacchetto compatto, non i documenti originali. Il registro host lega richiesta e risposta ma non certifica l’identità del modello. Senza risposta la revisione resta in attesa; la selezione alternativa Codex non si applica a Cowork.

Studio Archive delimita ogni esecuzione di questo processo e crea automaticamente un report dei dati inviati da Vera. Vera registra i propri invii; il report non ispeziona la chat o altri strumenti. Il report viene conservato sulla macchina anche quando tutti i dati sono stati inviati. I conteggi mancanti sono indicati come non determinabili. Il server riceve soltanto l’impronta del report e i riferimenti di verifica, associati al Vera userID della macchina, alla stessa esecuzione e alla revisione. Il contenuto del report e le evidenze restano locali.

security_controls.control: The audit entrypoint requires a portable Studio Archive context for the exact passive-invoice-audit workflow, verifies every external input against its immutable run receipt, and confines outputs to that customer run. Evaluation discovers the owning run from the result artifact and applies the same input and output boundary.

The workflow reads supplied invoice and ledger files without modifying them, writes only below the selected audit output directory, stages archive XML as content-addressed copies, and never exposes an ERP, filing, payment, or posting operation.

Ledger rows enter only through an explicit canonical-to-source header map. Every mapped monetary column uses the same reviewed number convention; accounting parentheses denote a negative amount, conflicting signs reject, and explicit zero never invokes missing-value fallback. Matching requires exact structured invoice references with corroborating supplier, date or amount evidence, or the exact supplier-date-amount combination; multiple candidates, duplicates, missing invoices and ledger orphans remain explicit instead of being forced.

Bounded XML parsing extracts structured FatturaPA fields and Decimal code performs invoice, VAT, ledger-total, balance, currency, duplicate and reference checks before semantic review; Luna is not used to replace mechanically exact arithmetic.

In Codex, the semantic adapter reuses the per-run verified journal-bank native Codex Seatbelt capsule, defaults to gpt-5.6-luna or uses an explicitly reviewed alternative, validates the configured effort and strict schema, supplies compact content over stdin, retains response/event/stderr/receipt evidence, fails closed on qualification or model mismatch, and contains no direct model API client or API-key path.

SQLite binds the audit to source, ledger, mapping, workflow and control digests; packet changes fail closed, completed content-addressed chunks are not repeated, interrupted chunks become pending, results are upserted by invoice ID, and content-bound chunk checkpoints plus validated native Luna artifacts recover results published immediately before interruption. Incomplete ordinary artifacts are preserved before retry and unsafe links fail closed. Explicit model selections and the complete review declaration bind the job fingerprint, native-artifact recovery and chunk checkpoints; a changed review cannot reuse the prior job. Runtime identity is bound to the job and checkpoints; native artifact recovery is limited to Codex. Missing Cowork responses remain awaiting_semantic_review, never successfully screened.

The XLSX workpaper contains professional-review exceptions and ledger orphans while full-population JSONL retains reconstruction evidence. The only non-exception label is no_issue_detected, which the workflow explicitly prevents from being described as correct, approved, verified or audit passed.

Synthetic evaluation accepts only an explicit mutation plan whose source is professionally labelled acceptable and already matched, unflagged and free of deterministic exceptions; it copies the packet to a separate output with a synthetic identifier, changes only booked account identifiers and descriptions while preserving ordinary line descriptions, retains original and replacement treatment, and never mutates the real ledger, packet, job database or source file.

An alternative worker model requires a reviewed-decision receipt bound to the workflow, model, effort and benchmark digest. CLI selection files are authorized engagement inputs. This checks a local review declaration, not reviewer authentication or benchmark quality; it never changes native host qualification or read boundaries. The default remains Luna. Configuration and review identity remain bound during replay and recovery. This option applies only to Codex; Cowork rejects Codex model-selection receipts and nondefault effort overrides.

The packaged Cowork agent requests Haiku with Read access and instructions limited to the exact request. The engine rejects symlink handoff files, wrong request/response digests, missing invocation identity, invalid result types or incomplete invoice coverage. These checks do not independently authenticate the host or enforce an OS read sandbox. The workflow does not invent usage, timing, model identity or review completion.

The v5 shared worker verifies live allow/deny filesystem canaries and required Codex exec capabilities inside the unchanged deny-default Seatbelt boundary. Actual OS build, Codex version and external executable digests are recorded per run without fixed release allowlists. Executables and runtime inputs are rechecked before output publication; concurrent changes reject the result. Historical v1–v4 records remain unchanged for receipt verification and cannot launch new work. No packet fields or external destination are added. Model/effort remain requested, not independently observed; JSONL does not prove hidden-tool absence.

Reviewed invoice inputs require a content-bound review declaration and exact original-file hashes within the population directory. Source or extraction changes reject reuse. The existing matching, arithmetic, currency checks, job binding and native worker boundary remain active.

Explicit Archive binding IDs and user/model-led source roles; public parser/mapping/matching qualification is immutable and content bound. Actor/tenant private draft CAS excludes confirmation. Reviewer-only signed scope and same-key durable intent precede the unchanged producer. Actual OS lease and owned global native write guard distinguish live ownership from stale markers; status does not inspect live worker capsules. Hard kill, missing ownership, guard cleanup failure or unreplayable job remains uncertain and preserves artifacts; no automatic restart. Prepared views replay sources, SQLite, JSONL, packets, checkpoints, summary and workbook. Only standard public output paths are offered, in private app metadata; capsule credentials, logs and SQLite sidecars are excluded. Binary previews contain metadata only. Reviewed CH-GE source-group preparation remains a specialist operation. No direct API, model substitution, ledger posting, signature, professional approval or Archive completion.

Reviewer-only signed current job/revision authority and private actor/tenant/run draft CAS govern exact invoice IDs and explicit human label choices. Draft recovery never restores confirmation or infers attribution. Registration retains the exact screening JSONL and immutable separate labels, review attribution and public evaluate_results output; previous versions remain sealed by four artifact hashes and readonly. Corrections preserve other pages and do not rewrite worker screening. Same-key durable intent precedes writes; foreign output changes, implementation changes or guard cleanup faults preserve actual files and an uncertain receipt, with no automatic retry. No real ledger posting, professional approval or Archive completion is implied.

model_processing.destination: OpenAI model processing used by Codex
Anthropic model processing used by Cowork

external_boundaries.content: Published shared package names and version constraints plus ordinary package-index request metadata. No client files, prompts, case data, credentials, or generated work are sent by this runtime installer.
controls: Only published shared core and explicitly selected OCR recipes are installed; package names are never derived from client material or prompts.

Host network denials stop package retrieval. Retry only the same declared setup after the host user or administrator authorizes registry access; never change host network settings or use an alternate installer to evade a denial.

Readiness probes the managed CPython 3.12 interpreter locally with isolated Python and site loading disabled, checks completed installation metadata, then checks the selected declared package versions and component imports in that interpreter. Recipe revisions, backend bytes and historical platform labels do not block a compatible environment. Compatible reuse leaves installation receipts unchanged; actual missing or incompatible dependencies require serialized repair.
All three products and their modules use the same environment. Optional OCR requires approval and is then retained in that environment. A shared environment is not a boundary between client matters.
external_boundaries.destination: Python Package Index (PyPI) or the package index configured for the active Python interpreter
external_boundaries.purpose: Prepare the published shared Vera, Clara and Lucia core requirements and explicitly approved optional OCR in one user-scoped Python 3.12 environment per operating-system host.
external_boundaries.retention: Packages remain in one fixed user-scoped environment outside plugin source and client folders until explicitly removed. The default location is ~/.local/share/mparanza/runtime/venv on macOS and Linux, and LOCALAPPDATA/mpr/venv on Windows; MPARANZA_RUNTIME_ROOT may override the parent. Enabled OCR remains enabled across later core updates. Package-index request-log retention is controlled by the configured index. Failed updates invalidate the readiness receipt and require repair before execution; this shared environment has no retained generations.

external_boundaries.content: The fixed CPython 3.12 version request, operating-system and architecture selection, and ordinary download request metadata. Setup does not read client files or add prompts, case material or generated reports to this request.
controls: Use an installed CPython 3.12 when available; otherwise use uv or automatically download the published uv 0.12.10 wheel, verify its pinned SHA-256, and provision private CPython 3.12 without changing system Python or shell profiles.
Probe the selected interpreter before creating the dependency environment; never fall back to executing workflows with another Python minor version.
A failed download or interpreter probe stops setup; existing environments and client files remain intact.
external_boundaries.destination: PyPI files.pythonhosted.org for the pinned uv bootstrap, and Astral python-build-standalone CPython distributions on GitHub
external_boundaries.purpose: Provision the single supported CPython 3.12 interpreter when it is absent, automatically bootstrapping uv if needed
external_boundaries.retention: When uv must be bootstrapped, the bootstrap executable and private interpreter remain inside shared runtime storage until removed. Download request-log retention is controlled by the providers.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Vera/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis.
controls: Only closed technical transport schemas are accepted; unknown fields and arbitrary recovery commands are rejected.
The fixed HTTPS transport refuses redirects. Reporting failures retain the outbox and do not discard professional outputs.
The remote connector is independent of local command-process startup. If the host cannot expose/connect it, no successful report is claimed.
Only two built-in setup/preparation retries may execute automatically, once per remedy revision. Client documents, ACLs and security settings are not changed.
A published update is not recovery. The failed operation must actually execute successfully before that installation delivery closes.

Supplemental diagnostics require ownership of the original report and matching execution metadata; they are stored separately and cannot change the original report UUID, delivery status or remedy revision. Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.
Actionable remedies target an explicit original report. Each delivery uses its own applicable revision; a different report with the same generic signal does not inherit that remedy.

A cached actual connector status permits only the two fixed retries for an existing matching local receipt and latest report. It performs no direct HTTP polling or identity adoption. Missing local receipts cannot be fabricated to authorise a retry.

A helper success records readiness. Host AI verification of the original task and inputs is required for all recovered outcomes, including setup/startup. Delayed failures cannot reopen an already recovered episode.
Failed fixed retries retain complete stderr privately for semantic review. Raw recovery stderr is not automatically transmitted.

An explicitly selected MPARANZA_INCIDENT_DELIVERY=local-only setting blocks automatic client HTTP transport for this execution while preserving local evidence. Incident queues are durably marked and not automatically flushed later; this does not make model-provider processing local-only.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza HTTPS operational-incident API and Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
external_boundaries.purpose: Diagnose observed execution/setup failures, return installation-specific remedies and receive actual recovery outcomes
external_boundaries.retention: Local capability, pending reports and receipts persist outside client folders. The service retains incident, report, remedy and outcome records; no automatic deletion period is enforced. Status access is scoped by the opaque capability. Pending diagnostic pointers and raw stderr persist in the private incident directory until a matching actual recorded supplementation receipt is acknowledged; unsuccessful review or delivery retains them. Supplementation never replaces the original recovery episode or reopens recovered records. Recorded original/outcome receipts can acknowledge only their exact local queued UUID without replacing the local capability or saved connector identity. Remedy revisions are retained from the surviving migration revision onward; overwritten legacy revisions are not reconstructed.

security_controls.control: Setup validates package-relative selections and installs the published shared recipe. No package names or dependency instructions are accepted from client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unknown module, missing requirements file, invalid target, or failed dependency validation stops the helper instead of executing it in a partial environment.

security_controls.control: One fixed environment is located outside plugin source and client folders. An exclusive operating-system installation lock waits for running managed Python readers, which hold a shared lease through a startup hook. Setup removes the ready receipt before mutation and restores it only after pip check and component validation. Failed setup leaves execution unavailable until repair. Symlink roots, locks and metadata are rejected. The installer is launched from base Python to avoid self-deadlock. This lease is concurrency protection, not a security sandbox. Other historical environments are not automatically deleted. State metadata normally uses atomic replacement. Only EXDEV or Windows error 17 falls back under the same installer lock to a single-link regular-file write with full-byte writes and fsync. Failed writes attempt to restore existing metadata or remove a newly created file; the ready receipt remains invalid until setup succeeds. This fallback is local and does not add a recipient or payload.
security_controls.on_violation: A target creation or validation failure returns a bounded setup error and the requested helper is not run.

security_controls.control: The Windows archive launcher probes a callable interpreter and package entrypoint without changing aliases, registry, execution policy or client folders. The archive helper checks package readability before setup and supplies an explicit task UUID to every managed archive command. Recovery requires reconnecting the selected existing archive root; tasks do not silently adopt each other's configuration. Diagnostics return bounded package/startup status rather than client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unreadable package or invalid session stops before runtime setup and archive commands.

security_controls.control: For the six explicitly supported assured modules, the launchers verify the complete package inventory and stable regular-file bytes against the embedded build-generated SHA-256 index. Symlinks, reparse entries, special files, extra directories/files, missing or changed code and unstable reads stop preparation. Unchanged hardlinked package code is materialized into a fresh private OS temporary directory; each copied file is re-read and must have one physical link, then the unchanged component integrity validator must pass. The managed installation and aliases are not modified. The copy contains indexed product code/assets, not client documents, credentials, workflow reports or dependency environments. This local index detects package drift; it is not a publisher signature, a signed origin attestation or proof of installed-host acceptance. Successful code copies remain in OS temporary storage for normal OS cleanup. The root-level host .in_use directory is non-executable bookkeeping: only ASCII numeric, ordinary single-link regular marker files are excluded from the product inventory. Nested directories, links, reparse points and non-numeric names there are rejected. Marker contents are not read, executed, transmitted or included in a recovery copy; host markers and installed product files are not modified.
security_controls.on_violation: Preparation failures and host permission denials stop execution. A failed private copy is removed; no installation chmod/unlink/manual repair, alternate sandbox or relaxed component validation is permitted.

security_controls.control: The parent Vera launcher reports a negative exit code or 137/247 as forced termination. It writes execution_failure.json only inside the selected workflow context output directory or its normalization/sample subdirectories; without that matching context it logs only. The diagnostic stores workflow/run identifiers, exit status and an explicit statement that memory exhaustion is not established by the exit code. It makes no model calls or network requests.
security_controls.on_violation: A worker failure remains failure; diagnostic persistence errors are logged rather than converted into a success.

security_controls.control: The standalone Python bootstrap passes uv only declared host paths, locale, proxy, CA and cache settings, preserving original environment-name casing. Unrelated token/API-key variables and inherited UV_*, VIRTUAL_ENV, CONDA_PREFIX, PYTHONHOME and PYTHONPATH are excluded; private UV_PYTHON_* and UV_CACHE_DIR values are set by the bootstrap. The same environment is used for interpreter discovery and its local probe.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from every bootstrap child process.

security_controls.control: The built-in incident dependency-setup retry uses the shared host/runtime environment allowlist, named runtime/state locations and recovery recursion guard instead of inheriting unrelated user tokens and keys.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from the child environment.

security_controls.control: When the maintained launcher itself runs under Python -I -B, it restores only its own resolved scripts directory for sibling technical-diagnostic imports. It does not add the caller working directory. Helper execution, diagnostic retention and explicit incident delivery policy remain unchanged.
security_controls.on_violation: The maintained launcher must stop rather than resolving technical diagnostics from the caller working directory.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Vera/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Saved anonymous connector authorization exchanges a random code with a PKCE verifier, client ID and fixed incident resource; the host saves access/refresh tokens. The server stores token/code hashes, technical callback metadata and a random connection UUID. No personal account signup, user profile, email or client-file permission is involved. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Installation-preparation failures submit only a fixed technical message, exception type/errno, or the indexed package-relative file name and expected/observed SHA-256 values for a content mismatch. No altered file contents or professional files are read for this report. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis. Current reporting-process version, protocol capabilities and server last-seen time are retained per process session, separately from historical failure versions; they do not establish that all conversations updated. Native-host binding, when invoked, accepts a random host UUID and scoped capability plus an optional explicit native-app label at the same incident service. Only the host capability hash is retained server-side. Stable app-profile UUIDs are derived from host UUID and app label; reporter-instance UUIDs may be task-local and do not count physical computers, plugin copies or people. App grouping grants no additional client status or outcome access. Operator views retain each original report, supplement, outcome and retry event with its actual reporting owner and server receipt time; missing historical task identity is not reconstructed. The native stdio identity bridge verifies its indexed entry, reporter, technical collector and product metadata, then executes an isolated temporary reporter snapshot using existing Python without installing dependencies. Its tool accepts only an existing reporter capability and sends host proof to the fixed register endpoint; it never returns the device key or copies the reporter key into the host identity file. Native broker version/session observations are retained separately from guest reporter and failure-worker observations. When native tools are not exposed in cloud Cowork, the saved remote connector continues to report under its distinct connection identity and physical-host linkage remains unknown; no device controls or folder permissions are expanded automatically. Native-helper failures return source-bound exception classes, errno or HTTP status, package-relative frames and developer-authored templates. Dynamic diagnostic values are not returned; unavailable capture is explicit. This bridge does not return raw stderr or device keys. The central recovery agent may request named technical evidence surfaces through a diagnostic-request remedy. The host AI replies with reviewed technical facts, the original report UUID and request revision. Original-task availability is represented by technical booleans, not task text, client identifiers or file contents. A resume remedy communicates a diagnosed correction to the existing authorized workflow; it does not carry executable code. Technical requests, response UUIDs, applicable revisions and their observed status are retained with the original episode. The central agent may implement and deploy incident-related software fixes through reviewed source and green CI under Fabio’s explicit recovery authorization; it does not receive professional case files or gain user-host permissions. Handled Studio Archive exceptions log their active traceback locally before returning the existing error JSON, allowing the same source-bound collector and host semantic review to retain their actual cause. The operator derives diagnostic publication, exact owner/report/revision receipt and reply states, the existing 15-minute deadline and reporting-owner last service contact from retained records. These delivery facts do not establish physical-host availability, diagnosis or original-task recovery. The operator also projects exact delivery, retry and original-task outcome evidence for all actionable remedy kinds, including software updates. Its 15-minute attention cadence is not an execution timeout. A local alert renderer uses technical incident facts and an AI-reviewed blocker, accountable next action, reason and scheduled check. An optional operator-maintained device label is accepted only with a recorded exact-device verification reference; it is not inferred from the recipient, OS or reporter identity. Rendered operator alerts may include opaque machine/case codes and a verified operator-device label, but no client contents, raw diagnostics, personal identifiers or credentials. The renderer neither sends email nor accesses the registry or client files. It rejects stale followup reviews and cannot assign an unreceived or overdue remedy back to the uncontacted Vera. Recovered labels require matching actual original-task success evidence; incomplete historical bindings remain unknown. The shared API also exposes a separate public workflow-testing endpoint: an allowlisted map of pipeline IDs to testing levels and baseline metadata, without incident details, computer IDs, run IDs or user feedback. Its reset is operator-only and does not change incident records. Native workflow transport supplies the same existing host proof during registration when it is available. The shared managed launcher also reports handled PDF recovery failures and subsequent attempts for journal-sampling and journal-bank-reconciliation. It projects fixed strategy/check identifiers, pass/fail/replay flags and attempt/readable-row counts only; PDF text, amounts, paths, adapter code and free-text rationale remain local. Supplements reuse the original report identity across process sessions and cannot certify original-task recovery. Other products carry the shared implementation but do not expose these journal workflows. Bank PDF inspection failures and subsequent corrections are linked per source, independently of journal failures. The bank source digest used in the episode key stays in local reporting state and is not added to transmitted evidence. Other bank statements cannot inherit that extraction recovery.
controls: Only closed technical transport schemas are accepted; unknown fields and arbitrary recovery commands are rejected.
The fixed HTTPS transport refuses redirects. Reporting failures retain the outbox and do not discard professional outputs.
The remote connector is independent of local command-process startup. If the host cannot expose/connect it, no successful report is claimed.
Only two built-in setup/preparation retries may execute automatically, once per remedy revision. Client documents, ACLs and security settings are not changed.
A published update is not recovery. The failed operation must actually execute successfully before that installation delivery closes.

The remote MCP requires OAuth access tokens for the fixed incident resource. Authorization uses S256 PKCE, exact registered callbacks and a single-use five-minute code. Refresh tokens rotate and a replay revokes the grant; raw OAuth credentials are never placed in model prompts or stored server records.

Supplemental diagnostics require ownership of the original report and matching execution metadata; they are stored separately and cannot change the original report UUID, delivery status or remedy revision. Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.
Actionable remedies target an explicit original report. Each delivery uses its own applicable revision; a different report with the same generic signal does not inherit that remedy.

A cached actual connector status permits only the two fixed retries for an existing matching local receipt and latest report. It performs no direct HTTP polling or identity adoption. Missing local receipts cannot be fabricated to authorise a retry.

A helper success records readiness. Host AI verification of the original task and inputs is required for all recovered outcomes, including setup/startup. Delayed failures cannot reopen an already recovered episode.
Failed fixed retries retain complete stderr privately for semantic review. Raw recovery stderr is not automatically transmitted.

Actual cached connector status reconciles only readiness hints bound to existing local report receipts. Readiness becomes action-required evidence rather than recovery; already recovered matching hints are cleared and unlinked hints are retained. No remote receipt is fabricated and no case inputs are inferred.

Before reporting an installation-preparation failure, the preflight verifies the reporting script, preflight script and product metadata against a stable build index, then snapshots them in a fresh private temporary directory and executes the reporter in isolated Python. Original-installation, cwd and PYTHONPATH imports are excluded. Damaged workflow code does not run. Unverifiable reporting components require the independent connector; queued delivery never implies recorded or recovered.

A diagnostic reply requires ownership and exact original execution metadata, plus a retained diagnostic-request revision targeting that original report. A late reply cannot answer a newer request. A diagnostic exchange cannot be marked recovered.

Operator publications can require the inspected current revision. Identical applicable remedies are idempotent and do not create another retry episode. Resume instructions use existing verified workflow tools and ordinary professional gates; service text is never executed as a command.

An explicitly selected MPARANZA_INCIDENT_DELIVERY=local-only setting blocks automatic client HTTP transport for this execution while preserving local evidence. Incident queues are durably marked and not automatically flushed later; this does not make model-provider processing local-only.

The shared implementation binds registrations, OAuth resources, task events, report signatures, feedback and update downloads to one product. Existing unmapped installations and receipt schema 1 remain Vera. Physical-computer identity is shared, while usage catalogues and testing epochs are separated by product.

PDF recovery evidence uses the existing durable outbox and exact original-report supplementation, including local-only delivery. Readable partial results and independent workflow gates survive incident-service failure. Frozen extraction is explicitly unqualified and never generates a recovered outcome.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza HTTPS operational-incident API and Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
external_boundaries.purpose: Diagnose observed execution/setup failures, return installation-specific remedies and receive actual recovery outcomes
external_boundaries.retention: Local capabilities, pending reports and receipts persist outside client folders. In tested Cowork task containers this filesystem is task-local; the saved host connection retains its separate random UUID and credentials. Access tokens last one hour; rotating refresh grants expire after 90 idle days and can be revoked. Token/code hashes and incident records have no automatic deletion period. Access requires the local capability or the saved connector token, with explicit capability proof before linking local reports. Pending diagnostic pointers and raw stderr persist in the private incident directory until a matching actual recorded supplementation receipt is acknowledged; unsuccessful review or delivery retains them. Supplementation never replaces the original recovery episode or reopens recovered records. Recorded original/outcome receipts can acknowledge only their exact local queued UUID without replacing the local capability or saved connector identity. Remedy revisions are retained from the surviving migration revision onward; overwritten legacy revisions are not reconstructed.

security_controls.control: Only a matching random installation capability can retrieve incident status or record its recovery. Stored keys are SHA-256 digests; server validation never echoes invalid input.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject without returning another installation record.

security_controls.control: Remote data cannot supply executable commands. Only reviewed built-in action IDs are supported; retries use argv without a shell and preserve integrity guards.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject unsupported actions and keep the incident open.

security_controls.control: OAuth discovery has fixed server URLs, public clients use mandatory S256 PKCE and exact registered callbacks, and every grant is bound to the incident resource and sole incident scope. Token/code hashes are stored, access expires in one hour, refresh rotates, reuse commits grant revocation, and foreign report outcomes require a proven local link. Caller-supplied metadata URLs are never fetched.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject invalid authorization, token or resource proof without returning caller inputs or another connection record.

security_controls.control: Built-in recovery children receive the shared host/runtime environment allowlist, explicit named runtime/state locations and the recovery recursion guard. Unrelated user tokens and keys are not inherited.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from the child environment.

external_boundaries.content: For every run of the 13 selected Vera pipelines, Archive automatically prepares a schema-3 proof request containing product, receipt UUID, plugin version, canonical report SHA-256, existing Vera userID (installation_id), Archive run ID and report revision. The operational transport authenticates existing installation credentials and requires its existing verified machine link. Ordinary connection metadata also reaches Mparanza. No report body, outgoing payloads, source paths, source hashes, row counts, source values, prompts or model outputs are submitted. Verification supplies the receipt ID, report hash, Vera userID, Archive run ID and revision together.
controls: Only the fixed 13-pipeline scope generates new automatic Vera reports. Every selected execution gets a report, including full exposure and incomplete measurements. Start/end writes control collection; no agent-authored report input or substantive-work decision is used.

Vera records its own outgoing CLI, MCP and model-worker payloads locally before sending them, independently of host hooks and transcripts. Private internal results and MCP app-only metadata are excluded. The terminal Archive write freezes the local report immediately; a later result from a still-running operation is withheld if its pinned run or revision has closed or changed.

Vera schema 3 requires authenticated installation credentials and an existing physical-machine link. The public anonymous stamping route cannot issue this schema. userID, Archive run ID, revision and report hash are included in the Ed25519 signature.

The request uses one fixed HTTPS operational endpoint. Additional fields, mismatched owner identity, changed retry evidence, wrong-product records and verification mismatches are rejected. Local outgoing payloads are never sent.

Retries retain identical report bytes, UUID, version and revision. Professional artifacts are checked before and after updating only the reserved reporting artifacts in the Archive seal. Ordinary Archive use retries pending receipts and interrupted terminal reporting without re-executing professional work.

An explicit local_only option or local onboarding marker suppresses the proof request but keeps the report. Network or identity failures retain a pending receipt without invalidating the professional work. Host permission denials remain binding.

Verification proves the stored report hash, authenticated Vera installation/machine binding, Archive run, revision and server time. It does not identify a natural person or establish provider-side receipt, correctness of measurements, analytical correctness or GDPR compliance.
Historical schema-1 and schema-2 receipts remain readable through their existing routes; the authenticated Archive proof does not depend on a separate workflow-usage link.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza's fixed HTTPS Vera run-receipt endpoint and public verification page
external_boundaries.purpose: Authenticate the existing machine Vera userID and bind the hash of each selected Archive run report to that run, revision and server time.
external_boundaries.retention: The server retains the proof fields, server timestamp, signature and signing-key identity, with a unique userID/run/revision binding, without an automatic deletion period. Reports, exact Vera outgoing payloads, local database and receipts remain inside the local Archive run until the studio removes them. Deleting a server proof makes later server verification unavailable.

security_controls.control: Both client and server enforce the same closed receipt request schema, and the server's Pydantic model forbids every unregistered field.
security_controls.on_violation: The request or response is rejected before a proof is accepted or written locally.

security_controls.control: Automatic Archive stamping and verification use fixed Mparanza HTTPS endpoints; operational credentials authenticate the existing Vera installation. The transport refuses redirects. The older generic receipt client retains its explicit loopback test option.
security_controls.on_violation: The client aborts before making a network request.

security_controls.control: The server signs the exact minimal record with Ed25519, including authenticated Vera userID, Archive run and revision for schema 3. A unique userID/run/revision binding prevents a second proof for different bytes. Conflicting receipt retries are rejected atomically; no report or source data are stored.
security_controls.on_violation: Missing keys make the service unavailable, invalid signatures are not returned as verified, and conflicting retries are rejected.

security_controls.control: Receipt routes cap body size and operation rates. Archive stamping additionally authenticates installation credentials and requires the retained verified device link; anonymous requests cannot create schema-3 proofs.
security_controls.on_violation: Oversized or excess requests receive an explicit 413 or 429 response without creating a receipt.

workflow-usage.display_name: Pipeline usage, outcomes and user satisfaction

external_boundaries.content: The existing installation capability authenticates closed-schema events: random run and event UUIDs, sequence, catalog pipeline ID, host, observed product version, timestamps, explicit user/synthetic/agent-test classification and started/resumed/completed/failed/cancelled state. Optional links contain only an existing signed receipt UUID/report digest or an owned incident report UUID. Run ownership, single-run receipt binding and the retained signature are checked server-side. The original stamping service does not attest the identity of the author of a report. The service receives no task text, client identity, filenames, source data, prompt or professional output. Existing connection metadata and rate limiting apply. Saved connector identity is not inferred to be a native computer. Native senders also present the existing anonymous native-computer capability and observed native app when available. The server retains the established computer binding; unlinked guests remain unlinked until an actual native proof is received. Connector-owned runs can obtain the bounded per-run proof described above; run-specific computer bindings are used by counts and completion indicators. No personal account information or hardware identifier is collected.
controls: Events are durably queued before transport and acknowledged by exact UUID, owner, sequence and hash. Interruptions stay outcome unknown; repeated submissions are idempotent.
Synthetic and agent-test runs are excluded from user metrics. Studio Archive is infrastructure and cannot be selected as a rated process.
The host AI selects the primary process and observes actual task completion. Counters and hashes do not assert professional correctness or independent model delivery.

The operational client honors an explicitly selected local-only HTTP delivery setting for this execution; this does not change synthetic-run exclusion, rating authorization or model-provider processing.

The shared implementation binds registrations, OAuth resources, task events, report signatures, feedback and update downloads to one product. Existing unmapped installations and receipt schema 1 remain Vera. Physical-computer identity is shared, while usage catalogues and testing epochs are separated by product.

Authenticated event acknowledgements and run status expose the original owner's proven Computer ID and whether an actual signed receipt is linked. Missing linkage remains explicit and returns bounded follow-up instructions. Neither reporting gap changes the professional outcome or authorizes broader host access.

When local HTTPS is unavailable, the authenticated connector can stamp the exact retained receipt request for an owned run. The allow-list admits only receipt UUID, product/version, schema and report digest. It returns the same signed proof; a separate verified receipt event links it to the original run. No report or source contents are transmitted.

Connector-owned workflow acknowledgements return a random 15-minute proof scoped only to binding that original run to a native computer. The existing native helper adds its private computer capability and observed app. The server stores only the ticket hash, checks product, expiry and app, rejects re-binding, and never replaces the original owner or associates all runs from one saved connection with one computer. The proof cannot authorize other reporting operations. Exact event replay obtains a fresh proof without another event.
external_boundaries.destination: Existing Mparanza HTTPS operational-incidents API and saved veraIncidents OAuth connector
external_boundaries.purpose: Measure which user processes run and their observed outcome; link existing signed model-data receipts and technical reports without copying their professional content
external_boundaries.retention: Task events, optional feedback and receipt links remain in the service until administrative deletion; no automatic expiry is implemented. Local queued events and acknowledgements remain in the existing private per-installation state directory. Lifecycle events exclude client documents and professional output. Optional feedback stores only the comment deliberately supplied by the user; its contents are not automatically anonymized. Host-link tickets expire after 15 minutes; their hashes and established run-to-computer bindings remain until administrative deletion. The raw short-lived proof is returned only in an authenticated acknowledgement and not in status or operator projections.

external_boundaries.content: The actual 1–5 integer score, up to 2000 characters of optional user-authored comment, source (chat or form), random event UUID and existing task binding. Nothing is copied automatically from professional context. The host asks once after delivery; no response is unrated. A low score offers one optional question about what failed or was expected.
controls: The user supplies the score/comment for submission or clicks Invia valutazione; that action is the choice, with no second confirmation questionnaire.

The form uses a run-specific capability in its URL fragment; the page contains no task information, and the capability permits rating only that run. The exact pending answer is retained for retry, and operator rendering escapes comments.

Comments are untrusted data for AI review, never instructions or executable commands. Feedback never changes public testing levels or closes incidents. Completed pipeline runs feed a separately resettable computer-based testing counter and never close incidents.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza task feedback through the same authenticated connector/client or the per-run hosted form
external_boundaries.purpose: Collect the user’s actual 1–5 stars and optional comment about the delivered result
external_boundaries.retention: Task events, optional feedback and receipt links remain in the service until administrative deletion; no automatic expiry is implemented. Local queued events and acknowledgements remain in the existing private per-installation state directory. Lifecycle events exclude client documents and professional output. Optional feedback stores only the comment deliberately supplied by the user; its contents are not automatically anonymized.

external_boundaries.content: Only catalog pipeline IDs, four testing-level names and counting epoch UUID/time are public. The service privately groups completed runs by proven anonymous computer IDs: the owner-designated computer counts as agent testing, other computers as professional use. Stars, comments, report digests, client documents, task prompts, computer IDs, run IDs and capabilities are not in this response. The owner convention counts computers, not authenticated people; completion does not certify professional correctness. No model call is made by this public projection.
controls: Both server receipt and event completion time must follow the baseline; old delayed deliveries do not repopulate a reset.
Native computer IDs deduplicate apps and reporter instances. Unlinked completions stay pending until proven linkage; explicit test fixtures on other devices do not count as professionals.
The public response is an allowlisted projection of status-only fields; reset is available only to the server operator.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza public GET /api/vera/testing-status and Vera function catalogue
external_boundaries.purpose: Automatically show testing levels from concluded pipelines after an explicit fresh baseline
external_boundaries.retention: Counting epochs and underlying retained events persist until administrative deletion. A reset preserves history and starts new public counts.

security_controls.control: Existing installation/OAuth authorization scopes task writes and reads; closed schemas reject unrelated fields. UUIDs, event order and retained hashes enforce retry identity.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject the event without changing task evidence.

security_controls.control: A usage receipt link must match the retained report digest/version and a valid server signature.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject the unverified link and retain the task without receipt evidence.

security_controls.control: The feedback route checks a per-run random capability, bounds the body and comment, and never exposes task data on the public form. Operator HTML escapes text.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject the request or render it only as literal text.

security_controls.control: The public endpoint returns only the four-state map and epoch metadata. Device/run identities and feedback remain private; no public reset route exists.
security_controls.on_violation: Unknown or missing fields are not included in the public projection.
